_doc: Expert prior suitability tables. host: index = DLR tree class (0 pine,1 spruce,2 douglas,3 larch,4 fir,5 beech,6 oak,7 birch,8 alder,9 other,10 canopy loss). nutrient: A,Z,M,K,R (half steps interpolated). water: 1 dry,2 mod. fresh,3 weakly gw-fresh,4 fresh,5 very fresh,6 damp,7 wet,8 swampy. unknown: factor used when the site map has no data for a forest cell. Weights are priors from field mycology, checked by pipeline/validate.py, not published constants.

species.lookalikes: Gallenröhrling (Tylopilus felleus): bitter, ruins a meal, pinkish pores and dark net on the stem. Taste a crumb raw and spit it out.
species.notes: Broad host range. Fruits mainly after warm rain in late summer.
Too few GBIF records in Berlin/Brandenburg to validate.

species.lookalikes: Gallenröhrling (bitter). Blue bruising of the pores is normal for this species.
species.notes: The most common bolete of Brandenburg pine forests.

species.lookalikes: Falscher Pfifferling (Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca): true gills, soft. Ölbaumtrichterling (Omphalotus): toxic, grows in clusters on wood.
species.notes: Rare in much of Brandenburg and sensitive to nitrogen deposition. This map over-predicts it.

species.lookalikes: Gallenröhrling (Tylopilus felleus), bitter. Other Leccinum species are edible when well cooked.
species.notes: Strictly with birch. Birches mixed into pine stands are invisible in the dominant-species map, so true habitat is wider than shown.

species.lookalikes: Must be cooked thoroughly (at least 20 min): raw or undercooked Rotkappen cause poisoning.
species.notes: Too few GBIF records to validate. Aspen Rotkappe not modelled: aspen is not in any tree map.

species.lookalikes: Other Suillus species, harmless. Peel the slimy cap skin, some people react to it.
species.notes: Pine only, prefers young stands and edges (stand age not modelled).
Poor dry pine sands, the classic Brandenburg Kiefernheide.

species.lookalikes: Hard to confuse. Grows at the base of old pines, often in the same spot each year.
species.notes: Needs old pines (stand age not modelled).

species.lookalikes: Young specimens can be confused with deadly Amanitas (Knollenblätterpilz). Only pick large caps with a snakeskin-patterned stem and a movable double ring. Safranschirmling causes stomach upset.
species.notes: Not tied to trees: modelled from forest edges, clearings and nutrient level. Low confidence.

excluded.why: Repeated meals cause rhabdomyolysis, deaths documented. Not presented as edible.
Spring micro-sites not captured by the data; deadly lookalike Gyromitra.
